summary: Case-sensitive byte-string comparison (strcmp-like) returning negative/zero/positive. Dispatches on the alignment of a1: a dword loop for 4-byte-aligned pointers, with byte and word prologues for misaligned pointers.

local_names.v4: current dword loaded from the source
local_names.v8: current word loaded in the misaligned prologue
local_names.v5: carry flag of the byte comparison (less-than)

operations.description: Alignment dispatch on a1: low bits zero selects the dword loop directly; bit0 set compares a leading byte then a word before entering the dword loop.
Dword loop: compares four bytes of *v2 against v3[0..3] per iteration, advances both pointers by 4, and stops on the first differing byte or on a zero byte.
Misaligned prologue: compares the byte at the odd start offset and the word at the next 2-byte boundary before the dword loop.
Returns 0 when a zero byte (string terminator) is reached, indicating equal prefixes.
Returns -2*carry + 1 on the first differing byte: negative if the source byte is smaller, positive if larger.

clean_pseudocode: if (a1 bit0 set) compare a1[0] vs a2[0];
compare word at next boundary vs a2;
dword_loop: compare 4 bytes at a time, stop on mismatch or NUL;
unresolved: Proposed name and the claimed relationship to 0045d4e0 (prelabel cluster_copy, DERIVED) not independently confirmed.
NUL-terminated semantics inferred from the zero-byte checks; terminator handling in the misaligned prologue not fully traced.
The dword path stops on an embedded null in either operand; whether both operands' terminators are handled symmetrically in all alignment cases is unclear.
The extracted fields this+0x0 and this+0x1 correspond to byte reads during the comparison but their class-level meaning is unknown.
